Job Summary

We are seeking a bilingual Community Program Coordinator for a direct hire opportunity with a nonprofit charitable organization in Redwood City, CA. This role is ideal for a community-focused professional who is passionate about outreach, language access, family support services, and helping prospective and existing family child care providers connect with valuable resources.

The Community Program Coordinator will support the Family Child Care Provider Pathways program by building relationships in the community, promoting available services, and helping providers access training, support, and program information. This is a great opportunity to join a mission-driven environment with supportive leadership, positive teamwork, and room for advancement. The location is convenient, with easy access near the freeway.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct community outreach and engagement to promote family child care provider programs, resources, and services.
Connect prospective and existing family child care providers with training, support services, and available community resources.
Provide bilingual English and Chinese language support, including verbal interpretation and translation of routine program materials.
Attend community events, outreach activities, and provider engagement opportunities throughout the local area.
Maintain accurate program records through data entry, administrative support, and follow-up communication.
Communicate professionally with diverse community members, providers, partner organizations, and internal team members.

Compensation And Benefits

Salary range: $55,000 to $60,000 per year.
Direct hire opportunity.

jobs.description:
Overview

We are hiring! We are seeking an energetic, highly motivated, and detail-oriented self-starter to join our geospatial team as a Senior
GIS Analyst
in our Ft. Lauderdale
office. Our ideal candidate will have education and experience with geospatial analysis, mapping processes, GIS software and technologies.

Under supervision, performs standard geographic information system (GIS) work while developing professional proficiency. Will work with an interdisciplinary group of GIS analysts, developers, and project managers out of client offices in Ft. Lauderdale (not remote).

Your role

Assist the Program Services section with the administration and maintenance of on premises ArcGIS Enterprise and ArcGIS Online.
Serve as the point of contact for various GIS projects/assignments.
Assist the Program Services section with maintaining the GIS applications, servers, layers, and feature classes for all FDOT District Four offices.
Attend requirement gathering and GIS coordination meetings.
Define project tasks and execute on those tasks.
Work with existing ArcGIS databases, datasets and applications to develop an understanding of their use and integration capabilities.
Develop solutions to ArcGIS needs using a combination of tools including app builders (ArcGIS Instant Apps, ArcGIS Dashboards, ArcGIS StoryMaps, and ArcGIS Experience Builder).
Work with FDOT ArcGIS Users developers, etc. to understand data landscape and needs.
Conducts data gathering, conversion and analysis of GIS data, prepares data documentation or metadata for GIS Projects, prepares maps and exhibits with GIS data sets, and participates in client needs analyses.
Maintains continued knowledge of technology developments in the GIS field and use of GIS software.
Performs such other duties as the Supervisor may from time to time deem necessary.
Write clear technical documentation to support data development work.
Collaborate with technical and nontechnical staff to understand client GIS needs .
Complete other tasks as assigned by the FDOT Manager.

B.A. or B.S. or M.S. in Geography, computer science, or GIS-related environmental discipline.
5 years of experience required with bachelor's degree; 3 year of experience required with master's degree.

jobs.title: Senior Data Analyst
jobs.description:
PermitFlow is redefining how America builds. We’re an applied AI company serving the nation’s builders, tackling one of the largest information challenges in the economy: understanding what can be built, where, and how . Our AI agent workforce helps the fastest-growing construction companies navigate everything from permitting and licensing to inspections and project closeouts – accelerating housing, clean-energy, and infrastructure development across the country.

Despite being a $1.6T industry, construction still suffers from massive delays, wasted capital, and lost opportunity. PermitFlow has already delivered unprecedented speed, accuracy, and visibility to over $20B in development, helping contractors reduce compliance time, de-risk projects, and scale with confidence.

As the U.S. enters a new capex supercycle across data centers, factories, housing, and renewables, joining PermitFlow means building the AI infrastructure at the core of every construction project driving the next wave of reindustrialization.

We’ve raised over $90M, most recently completing our Series B, from top-tier investors including Accel, Kleiner Perkins, Initialized, Y Combinator, Felicis, and Altos Ventures, with backing from leaders at OpenAI, Google, Procore, ServiceTitan, Zillow, PlanGrid, and Uber.

Our HQ is in New York City with a hybrid schedule (3 in-office days per week). We prefer NYC-based candidates or those open to relocation.

Role Overview

PermitFlow is looking for a Senior Data Analyst to be the dedicated analytics partner for our Customer Success and Operations teams - the teams that deliver permits to our customers every day. Your work will shape how leadership runs and scales these orgs. You'll partner with Operations Leaders, CSMs, and Analytics Engineers to turn open-ended questions into the reports, metrics, and dashboards the company runs on.

What You'll Do

Own analytics for Customer Success and Operations. Collaborate closely with senior leaders to understand their roadmaps, identify areas of opportunity, and help define and measure success. Your analyses will directly shape how we drive retention, speed up permit turnaround, and scale these teams.
Deliver tangible impact. Triage incoming requests for new data, charts, and metrics, push back on low-value asks, and focus analytics effort where it moves the business most.
Build to answer the next hundred questions. Turn recurring requests into dashboards that power self-serve analytics. Work with Analytics Engineering to write dbt models when the data isn't easily available, and own the documentation to make it easy to find in the future.
Be the translator. Take open-ended requests and turn them into PRDs, leading the way through ambiguous, high-impact problems.

What We're Looking For

3–5+ years in analytics, business intelligence, or a similar role where you used data to improve decision-making.
Strong SQL: CTEs, window functions, and the patience to work through a wide table you didn't build.
Experience modeling in a BI tool (Omni preferred), as well as a data warehouse like BigQuery or Snowflake.
Working knowledge of dbt: you can write a model, add tests, open a pull request, and have an eye for efficiency.
Hands-on use of LLM tools (Claude, Cursor, or similar) to write SQL faster, draft dbt models, and automate reporting.
The instinct to ask what decision a request is for before writing any SQL.
Bonus: Experience working with Salesforce data, supporting Customer Success or Operations teams, and/or modernizing legacy reporting to meet evolving business needs.

What We Offer

Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a high-growth company
100% company-paid base medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees + healthcare FSA
401(k) savings plan
Unlimited PTO and paid family leave
Home office & equipment stipend
Daily in-office lunch and dinner provided
Commuter benefits (pre-tax transit and parking)

PermitFlow provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or family status, as protected by applicable law.

We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities. All employment decisions are based on merit, qualifications, and business needs.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator (ACP)
jobs.description:
Job Summary

This position is located in the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants (OVSJG), Victim Services Division. The mission of the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants is to develop, fund, and coordinate programs that improve public safety; enhance the administration of justice; and create systems of care for crime victims, youth, and their families in the District. OVSJG supports and coordinates the development and implementation of a comprehensive system of care for crime victims within the District of Columbia. OVSJG advocates on behalf of victims at all levels of government and community; and works to ensure that comprehensive services are available in the District for victims of crime. The ACP program allows eligible individuals to receive mail at a confidential address and provide a legal substitute address for the individual's physical address on public records. The incumbent is responsible for administering the District's Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), which involves planning, research, data collection, analysis and evaluation, and providing training to community members and advocates.

Duties And Responsibilities

Supports the coordination of the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) activities in order to develop program policies, procedures, forms, and other materials. Identifies and collects performance metrics for OVSJG to report on the ACP in order to evaluate and address concerns regarding the efficiency and operation of the program. Reviews and provide recommendations on ACP applications to the Program Manager and agency leadership in order to streamline participant enrollment into the program. Interprets and provides guidance to leadership and advocates; advises on unclear or vague policies and procedures relating to the ACP. Identifies problems and specific issues in a particular area of ACP and advises the supervisor of existing problems in order to recommend solutions or alternatives for program implementation and supporting survivors. Develops and provides training to community-based organizations that serve as ACP application assistants for clients in order to aid in their enrollment into the program. Provides guidance and technical assistance to District agencies in order to implement the statutory requirements of the program.

Maintains records of any certified or registered mail received on behalf of a participant. Maintains information and documentation regarding the ACP databases to track actions and provide periodic reporting, or projects that relate to the program. Receives first-class, certified, and registered mail sent to a participant at a substitute address in order to forward mail to respective participants. Represents the program at community events; meets with individuals, community-based organizations, DC government agencies, etc.; participates in related conferences, meetings, and training seminars in order to report findings and essential information back to senior staff. Coordinates project phases with technical and professional stakeholders involved in the project. Provides information, as required by project specifications in order to communicate information and decisions concerning projects with all interested parties.

Qualifications And Education

This position requires at least one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level in the normal line of progression. Specialized experience is experience which is directly related to the position and has equipped the individual with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.

Licenses and Certifications

None.

Working Conditions/Environment

The work is primarily performed in offices.

Other Significant Facts

Tour of Duty:
Monday- Friday; 8:30 AM - 5 PM

Pay Plan, Series and Grade:
CS-0301-12

Promotion Potential:
No Known Promotion Potential

Duration of Appointment:
Career Service - Permanent

Collective Bargaining Unit:
This position is not covered under a collective bargaining unit.

Residency Preference:
When claiming residency
preference, you are required, and must agree in writing, to maintain bona fide District residency for a period of seven (7) consecutive years from the effective date of employment. You will be required to present documents (proofs) to show District residency and failure to maintain bona-fide District residency for the seven-year (7-year) period will result in forfeiture of employment

If you love helping patients, staying organized, and being part of a fast paced, supportive team… we want to meet you!

Conducts outreach with potential referring providers and works collaboratively with physician liaisons and related departments to increase referrals to the program.

Communicates with referring physicians regarding patient appropriateness for program and coordinates information with referral services.

Distributes patient letters, provides follow-up and confirmation calls and r esponsible for collecting and maintaining patient responses to program surveys. Responsible for maintaining the LCSP database, which includes data entry, patient letters, patient management activities and statistical reporting. 

Responsible for managing the National Lung Cancer Screening Registry including extracting data from operative reports, pathology reports and imaging and manually uploading into the ACR to maintain accreditation standards.

Prepares weekly program statistics. Provides updates on program activity, statistics, and recommendations for program enhancements.

Serves as an active member of the Lung Cancer Screening Program Steering committee and as an ad-hoc member to the Thoracic Tumor Board committee. Serves as an ad-hoc member to the Lung Cancer Tumor Board team.

Ensures all accreditation requirements are adhered to, gathers, and submits required data in a timely fashion.

Coordinates with Patient Financial Services and the Finance Department as needed.  Assists in tracking the financial impact of program.  Prepares analytical data as requested.

Helps plan and organize community outreach events, working collaboratively with THOfNE department such as Community Health and Wellness, Oncology, and other departments. Offsite work and hours may occasionally apply.  Assists in the planning of specialized lung cancer and smoking cessation events and programs during key times of the year including lung cancer awareness month.

Provides cross-coverage to the thoracic surgery clinic and oncology clinic as needed.

 Monday - Friday; hours can be flexible around start/end times

:
Minimally requires a high school diploma or equivalent.  Associate’s degree in related field is preferred.  Medical Assistant and/or certified tumor registrar (CTR) preferred.

A minimum of three (3) years of progressive relevant experience in a healthcare environment. Previous experience in Pulmonary Medicine, Oncology or Diagnostic Imaging preferred.   Prior experience in scheduling preferred.

Advanced knowledge of computer systems, Microsoft office-Word, PowerPoint, Excel, etc.  Requires exceptional data entry skills.

Strong organizational and interpersonal skills. Demonstrates attention to detail. Presentation skills required.

Strong customer service skills required.  Excellent communication skills required to interact with all levels of Clinic personnel.   Ability to take initiative and work independently with minimum supervision.

PermitFlow is redefining how America builds. We’re an applied AI company serving the nation’s builders, tackling one of the largest information challenges in the economy: understanding what can be built, where, and how . Our AI agent workforce helps the fastest-growing construction companies navigate everything from permitting and licensing to inspections and project closeouts – accelerating housing, clean-energy, and infrastructure development across the country.

Despite being a $1.6T industry, construction still suffers from massive delays, wasted capital, and lost opportunity. PermitFlow has already delivered unprecedented speed, accuracy, and visibility to over $20B in development, helping contractors reduce compliance time, de-risk projects, and scale with confidence.

As the U.S. enters a new capex supercycle across data centers, factories, housing, and renewables, joining PermitFlow means building the AI infrastructure at the core of every construction project driving the next wave of reindustrialization.

We’ve raised over $90M, most recently completing our Series B, from top-tier investors including Accel, Kleiner Perkins, Initialized, Y Combinator, Felicis, and Altos Ventures, with backing from leaders at OpenAI, Google, Procore, ServiceTitan, Zillow, PlanGrid, and Uber.

Our HQ is in New York City with a hybrid schedule (3 in-office days per week). We prefer NYC-based candidates or those open to relocation.

Role Overview

PermitFlow is looking for a Senior Data Analyst to be the dedicated analytics partner for our Customer Success and Operations teams - the teams that deliver permits to our customers every day. Your work will shape how leadership runs and scales these orgs. You'll partner with Operations Leaders, CSMs, and Analytics Engineers to turn open-ended questions into the reports, metrics, and dashboards the company runs on.

What You'll Do

Own analytics for Customer Success and Operations. Collaborate closely with senior leaders to understand their roadmaps, identify areas of opportunity, and help define and measure success. Your analyses will directly shape how we drive retention, speed up permit turnaround, and scale these teams.
Deliver tangible impact. Triage incoming requests for new data, charts, and metrics, push back on low-value asks, and focus analytics effort where it moves the business most.
Build to answer the next hundred questions. Turn recurring requests into dashboards that power self-serve analytics. Work with Analytics Engineering to write dbt models when the data isn't easily available, and own the documentation to make it easy to find in the future.
Be the translator. Take open-ended requests and turn them into PRDs, leading the way through ambiguous, high-impact problems.

What We're Looking For

3–5+ years in analytics, business intelligence, or a similar role where you used data to improve decision-making.
Strong SQL: CTEs, window functions, and the patience to work through a wide table you didn't build.
Experience modeling in a BI tool (Omni preferred), as well as a data warehouse like BigQuery or Snowflake.
Working knowledge of dbt: you can write a model, add tests, open a pull request, and have an eye for efficiency.
Hands-on use of LLM tools (Claude, Cursor, or similar) to write SQL faster, draft dbt models, and automate reporting.
The instinct to ask what decision a request is for before writing any SQL.
Bonus: Experience working with Salesforce data, supporting Customer Success or Operations teams, and/or modernizing legacy reporting to meet evolving business needs.

What We Offer

Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a high-growth company
100% company-paid base medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees + healthcare FSA
401(k) savings plan
Unlimited PTO and paid family leave
Home office & equipment stipend
Daily in-office lunch and dinner provided
Commuter benefits (pre-tax transit and parking)
